markdown_report:
**Evidence and insights.** The starting recent-mean residual supplies an inexpensive recent-interest path. A global scalar cannot adapt across contexts, but adaptive routing must outperform scalar controls. Electronics misranks 21.89% of fitted pairs; recent deletion changes fitted HR@10 by zero. This motivates discrimination experiments without identifying a popularity shortcut. Movies loses 0.155 fitted HR@10 after recent deletion, supporting preservation of its existing sequential encoder. Neither fitted margins nor embedding alignment establishes generalization or collapse.

Three literature insights refine the proposal. [Sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) motivates objective controls because sampling changes difficulty and popularity behavior. [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152), [SDM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00385), and [MQSA-TED](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056) establish precedents for transitions, temporal fusion, and transition-enhanced sequence modeling. [MoS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20858) motivates contextual routing, although additional complexity needs evidence at 10% research progress.

**Framework and candidates.** Organize methods along three axes: discrimination objective, directional representation, and temporal routing. SASRec already models recent and older dependencies; the residual adds an order-insensitive recent summary and a directional candidate interaction.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Positive and negative assessments for every dimension appear in the implementation notes.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A: Uniform 32-negative candidate CE | 2/7/4/8/4 | Clean discrimination control; current intent remains implicit. |
| B: Adaptive directional recent residual + A | 3/7/7/8/6 | Explicit recent transition path; established components and sparse supervision limit claims. |
| C: Randomly initialized title-token features added to B | 4/7/8/6/7 | Shares content evidence across sparse items; lexical associations can reproduce broad similarity. |

**Selected: B.** Retain B as the eligible research hypothesis; implement A first as its necessary control. B targets two user failures: stale history dominating immediate preference, and broad associations outranking specific recent connections. Its asymmetric score learns follow-on associations, not compatibility, complementarity, or ownership needs. Candidate CE addresses Electronics’ weak fitted separation, without guaranteeing validation improvement.

```python
h = sasrec(sequence)
r = causal_recent_mean(item_emb(sequence), window=3)
g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r, log1p(prefix_length))))
score = dot(h, item_emb(candidates)) + g * dot(source(r), target(candidates))
loss = cross_entropy(score, positive_index=0)
```

Use 32 unique uniform negatives excluding complete training history, padding, and the target; specify loss scaling, initialization, and reproducible sampling below. Primary controls remain baseline, CE-only, residual-only, and combined. Further scalar-gate, capacity, and symmetry controls are conditional on budget; absent controls limit mechanism claims.

Prespecify checkpoints, stopping, and tie-breaking. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; report paired within-category bootstrap macro differences if host user outcomes are available. Intervals exclude adaptive-selection bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Preserve the sampled evaluator: sampled and full-catalog rankings can differ ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Update predictor generation and diagnostic interfaces together. Report realized residual contributions rather than interpreting gate magnitude as reliance. No improvement is measured.

idea.description: Add a context-gated, low-rank directional recent-history score residual to each per-dataset SASRec and train with uniform 32-negative candidate-set cross-entropy. Preserve SASRec’s sequential score and test whether contextual gating adds value beyond the existing scalar recent-mean residual and objective-only controls.
idea.motivation: Explicitly target stale historical influence and broad similarity displacing specific recent interests. Address Electronics’ model-facing weak fitted positive–negative separation. These are hypotheses: history insensitivity does not establish popularity shortcuts, and directional interaction supervision does not establish compatibility, complementarity, substitution, immediate need, or ownership satisfaction. At 10% research progress, implement the objective-only control first and retain the combined method only if pinned macro validation HR@10 supports it.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture: inherit and serialize every RecHarness SASRec architecture setting. At each supervised position t, calculate h_t using the causal encoder and r_t as the mean of up to the last three nonpadding input item embeddings through t, never future inputs or targets. This mean is order-insensitive within its window; h_t remains order-sensitive and already includes both recent and older context. Set projection rank k=max(1,floor(d/4)); use independent bias-free Linear(d,k) source and target projections with Xavier initialization. Define g_t=sigmoid(w^T[h_t;r_t;log1p(n_t)]+b), where n_t counts observed nonpadding events through t, w starts at zero, and b=-2. Score candidate j as h_t^T e_j + g_t source(r_t)^T target(e_j). Use raw embeddings, temperature 1, and no additional normalization or residual-only dropout. Gate bias is an initialization choice, not a guarantee that the initial residual is small relative to the base score. Serialize the complete configuration, parameters, optimizer state, and random-generator states.

Sampling: preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; initialize explicit sampling generators with 42 and save their states. Construct sorted eligible IDs from the route’s catalog excluding padding and the user’s complete training history. Also exclude the current positive explicitly. Draw exactly 32 unique uniform negatives independently for every valid target position, without replacement within a position; overlap between positions is permitted. Fail explicitly if fewer than 32 eligible IDs exist rather than silently changing the objective. Sampling through randperm over sorted eligible IDs defines the reference distribution; an optimized sampler must preserve that distribution. Complete-training-history exclusion uses training information only and does not consult validation or test labels. Because train_loader currently yields a None user field, extend the training data pipeline to retain aligned user identities internally, while preserving the required diagnostic loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative). Do not infer identities from sequences or silently exclude only the visible prefix.

Loss and optimization: flatten all M valid nonpadding target positions. Candidate column zero is the positive, followed by its 32 negatives. Sum float32 cross-entropy over positions and divide by M. If scoring in chunks, sample all candidate IDs before scoring so chunk size does not alter RNG consumption; backpropagate each chunk’s sum/M immediately, retaining the shared encoder graph until the final chunk, then perform one optimizer step. Benchmark a practical chunk size within the trial budget. Candidate CE is a restricted ranking objective, not an unbiased approximation to full-catalog softmax: eligible-item inclusion probability is 32/|E_u|. The BCE control is mean_t[softplus(-s_positive)+softplus(s_negative)] using one identically eligible uniform negative per position. Averaging both labels would halve this scale. Inherit baseline optimizer, learning rate, regularization, batch size, and encoder initialization settings for the initial controlled comparison, and save their resolved values. Differences in loss scale can alter optimization; any subsequent learning-rate or regularization tuning must receive comparable budgets and be logged as additional trials. Dot-product and projection norms can change effective sharpness despite fixed temperature.

Experiments and selection: retain the four primary controls: original SASRec with BCE; SASRec with CE; directional adaptive residual with BCE; and the residual with CE. This original SASRec control is distinct from the supplied scalar recent-mean starting idea. Compare that starting idea as an additional control if budget permits; otherwise explicitly leave its incremental comparison unresolved. Apply one prespecified schedule across primary trials: SASREC_EPOCHS defaults to 200, evaluate every 20 epochs and at the completed final epoch, and use no validation-patience stopping. Allocate at most 10,800 GPU-seconds to each primary trial, including its training, evaluation, diagnostics, and failures, within the shared 43,200 GPU-second ceiling. Stop cleanly at the time cap; compare curves at matched cumulative GPU-seconds and retain every attempted trial. Use the highest host-reported four-category macro validation HR@10 among eligible checkpoints; break checkpoint ties by the earlier epoch, and model ties by fewer added parameters, then a fixed recorded trial order. If the host does not support intermediate checkpoint evaluation, use only its supported final evaluation and document that restriction without modifying its evaluator. Any extra tuning or controls must fit remaining shared budget rather than assume additional compute. Prespecification reduces flexibility but cannot remove optimism from adaptive selection.

Conditional mechanism controls: retrain fixed gates 0, 0.5, and 1, a learned global scalar, and the context gate under matched settings and comparable budgets. Compare an equally sized SASRec scoring adapter to investigate extra capacity. For directionality compare the asymmetric M=A^T B with a symmetric signed factorization Q^T D Q, matching rank and parameter count as closely as practical; A^T A additionally imposes positive semidefiniteness and is an incomplete symmetry control. Gate shuffling and residual removal at inference assess intervention sensitivity; distinguish them from retrained ablations. Without these controls, describe the combined method’s measured performance only, not an established routing or directionality mechanism.

Diagnostics: preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions and using both in the prompt. Keep view.model as the trained nn.Module and view.item_emb compatible. Make log2feats return a documented packed tensor containing h_t and v_t=g_t source(r_t); predict_score then computes h_t^T e_j+v_t^T target(e_j). Update all feature-dimension assumptions accordingly and verify that diagnostic, training, and generated prediction scoring agree. Return fitted_recent_gate=null because there is no scalar gate parameter; report adaptive-gate summaries separately. Projection scale can offset gate magnitude, so measure candidate-centered residual RMS relative to base RMS, positive–negative margin contributions, branch correlation, and rank/top-10 changes, with explicit candidate sets and null handling for zero denominators. Retain embedding-geometry and fitted-margin definitions without calling alignment collapse or comparing raw margin scales as calibrated accuracy. Preserve the supplied fitted-reliance limitations: targets participated in training; compact deletion changes length, positions, and adjacency; no causal preference or held-out claims follow. Position-preserving removal stays unavailable unless query/key/value masks are verified.

Evaluation uncertainty and shortcuts: if the host exposes paired per-user validation hits, bootstrap 2,000 times with seed 42, independently resampling 200 users within each category while keeping each user’s model outcomes and candidates paired, then average category differences equally. Report category deltas and the macro percentile interval; it conditions on fitted models, seed, and candidates and excludes training variability and adaptive-selection bias. If these outcomes are unavailable, report uncertainty as unavailable rather than reconstructing or altering the host evaluator. Evaluate training-only popularity, last-item transition, and order-agnostic recent-history controls on identical fitted-probe candidates where budget allows. Report popularity/history-length breakdowns with counts. For the required 20 training users, separately describe full-catalog unseen-item coverage, popularity, concentration, and inter-user overlap; these do not measure held-out accuracy, satisfaction, diversity preference, or conformity. The sampled 99-negative benchmark remains the selection target, even if full-catalog diagnostic behavior differs.

Deployment and constraints: retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, and trial-local artifacts. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the same gate, projections, causal pooling, padding behavior, and scoring equation. Save resolved software/device settings, iteration order, seeds, determinism settings, configuration, checkpoints, and costs. Use deterministic operations where supported and record any limitations; do not claim cross-device bitwise reproducibility. Available optional content consists only of public titles, descriptions, histories, and timestamps. Do not use unavailable reviews, ratings, product categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits, and do not fetch pretrained weights.

Dimension-specific assessments, scores on 0–10: A originality 2: positive—isolates candidate competition; negative—standard sampled objective. A potential 7: positive—useful scalable baseline; negative—sampler gains can be benchmark-specific. A user alignment 4: positive—may improve top-list discrimination; negative—does not explicitly encode current purpose. A model alignment 8: positive—directly targets weak fitted separation; negative—training separation may not transfer. A difficulty 4: positive—encoder remains unchanged; negative—user-aware unique sampling and memory-safe scoring require integration. B originality 3: positive—compact context-gated transition extension of the starting point; negative—transition fusion and temporal gates have substantial precedent. B potential 7: positive—clear extensions and component tests; negative—sparsity and routing shortcuts can limit transfer. B user alignment 7: positive—explicitly addresses stale-history influence and nonspecific associations; negative—cannot identify ownership needs or compatibility. B model alignment 8: positive—combines candidate discrimination with a recent-history path; negative—history sensitivity is not itself a quality target. B difficulty 6: positive—few additional trainable modules; negative—sampling, predictor generation, diagnostics, and controlled experiments must remain consistent. C originality 4: positive—shares task-trained text evidence with directional transitions; negative—content-aware recommendation is established. C potential 7: positive—could support sparse items; negative—text quality and token sparsity may dominate. C user alignment 8: positive—can expose specific content connections and improve identifiable relevance; negative—text similarity does not establish suitable use. C model alignment 6: positive—parameter sharing may improve sparse-item learning; negative—no supplied diagnostic isolates missing text as a cause. C difficulty 7: positive—requires no external model; negative—training-only vocabulary construction, tokenization, pooling, and synchronized inference add complexity. C remains a future extension, not part of B or a measured improvement.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify configuration, trial order, checkpoints, tie-breaking, and total GPU budget.
For each of baseline-BCE, CE-only, residual-BCE, residual-CE:
  For each prescribed dataset route:
    Load unchanged splits using preprocessing seed 0.
    Seed initialization and explicit sampling generators with 42.
    Resolve and save inherited SASRec and optimizer settings.
    Build sorted training-only eligible catalogs indexed by training user.
    Initialize the required encoder, projections, and gate.
    For each batch, retaining aligned user IDs internally:
      h = causal SASRec features(sequence)
      r = causal mean of up to three latest nonpadding input embeddings
      n = cumulative nonpadding input count
      g = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, r, log1p(n))))
      Flatten valid positions and sample candidates before chunking.
      Require 32 unique eligible negatives for CE, or one for BCE.
      For each position chunk:
        base = dot(h, item_emb(candidate_ids))
        residual = g * dot(source(r), target(item_emb(candidate_ids))) if enabled else 0
        score = base + residual
        Backpropagate the chunk loss sum / total valid positions.
      Step the optimizer once after all chunks.
    Save scheduled checkpoints and complete reproducibility state within the trial cap.
  Generate predictor code with identical four-route architecture and scoring.
  Obtain only host-supported pinned validation scores.
  Record all costs, failed trials, category scores, and learning curves.
Select using macro validation HR@10 and prespecified ties.
Run budgeted compatible diagnostics; label fitted and full-catalog descriptive probes explicitly.
If paired host validation outcomes are available, report category and macro paired bootstrap differences.
Do not claim improvement, causal reliance, or mechanism identification without the corresponding evidence.

originality.positive: Provides a compact context-gated transition residual tailored to the supplied SASRec starting point, with separable objective and architecture controls.
originality.negative: Asymmetric transitions, short/long-interest fusion, and learned gates have established precedents in FPMC, FOSSIL, SDM, and subsequent sequential recommenders.

future_potential.positive: Creates a manageable foundation for later timestamp-conditioned routing and task-trained public-text sharing, with explicit controls for each addition.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions, finite validation selection, and popularity or recent-item shortcuts may limit transfer; no gain has been measured.

code_difficulty.positive: The model extension needs only causal pooling, two low-rank projections, and one contextual gate.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible user-specific negative sampling, chunked gradients, predictor generation, diagnostic adaptation, and compute-matched controls add substantial integration work.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequential encoder retained by the proposed method.
Models both recent and longer-range dependencies; its features should not be labeled purely long-term.
limitations: Learned item IDs alone do not establish product compatibility or reliably represent items without training interactions.
The supplied fitted diagnostics do not establish its held-out failure mechanism.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: Compares sampling strategies and motivates separating objective changes from architecture changes.
Supports checking accuracy and popularity behavior together.
limitations: Reported tradeoffs do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Sampling changes can introduce false negatives and different optimization difficulty.

related_work.title: MQSA-TED
contributions: Combines temporal attention queries with global transition information, motivating a directional recent-history branch.
limitations: Transition evidence can be weak under sparsity.
Transitions do not label complementarity, substitution, or compatibility.

related_work.title: MoS
contributions: Uses multiple interest views and routing to address shifting and recurring interests.
limitations: Its full expert architecture exceeds the selected minimal extension.
Transfer to this benchmark remains unmeasured.

related_work.title: FOSSIL: Factored Sequential Prediction with Item Similarity Models
contributions: Combines historical item similarity with personalized higher-order Markov dynamics.
Establishes precedent for combining persistent preferences and sequential transitions.
limitations: Provides architectural precedent rather than evidence for the proposed contextual gate.
Observed transitions do not identify practical ownership needs.

related_work.title: SDM: Sequential Deep Matching Model for Online Large-scale Recommender System
contributions: Establishes learned gating between short-term and long-term representations.
limitations: Reduces the originality attributable to adaptive temporal fusion.
Its system setting does not establish results under the prescribed four-category evaluation.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains why repeated model and checkpoint selection can overfit finite validation data.
Motivates prespecified selection rules and complete trial accounting.
limitations: Paired user bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive-selection bias or capture training-seed variability.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.
Full-catalog diagnostics on 20 training users cannot substitute for held-out evaluation.

related_work.title: PyTorch sampling, determinism, and cross-entropy documentation
contributions: Documents candidate-class cross-entropy and reduction semantics.
Companion documentation for torch.multinomial and torch.use_deterministic_algorithms supports explicit sampling and reproducibility settings.
limitations: Correct API use does not make restricted candidate CE an unbiased full-softmax estimator.
Determinism settings do not guarantee identical results across software versions or devices.
